text:
maria: Heads-up — eu-west1 just had a provisioning wave (3k short-lived GPU jobs). Seeing scratch NVMe slot starvation, GPU attaches piling up. Anyone oncall? :eyes:
liam: i'm on it. `iostat -x 1 3` shows a sustained iops spike on /dev/nvme0n1, avg util ~99%, rrqm/s up. looks like janitor/scrub jobs coincided with the attach wave.
sre-bot: ALERT: nodepool-eu-west1-scratch utilization > 92% for 12m. attach-queue depth 184. affected services: gpu-provisioner, batch-orchestrator.
anya: we saw a similar pattern last month but this one is more bursty — scrub windows aligned after an autoscale. do we have scrub start jitter enabled?
liam: scrub start jitter is off for this pool (it was a canary config). all nodes started scrub at the 00s boundary after scale. that created concentrated iops pressure and slot exhaustion.
maria: ugh. so two things: 1) janitor/scrub storms; 2) attach admission not gating on free_scratch_slots properly.
jordan: quick mitigation: reduce janitor concurrency and pause expensive deep-scrubs on nodes that are >80% busy. can push via feature-flag: `janitor.deepScrubConcurrency=1` and `janitor.skipDeepScrubIfScratchBusy=true`.
liam: i'm rolling a hotfix patch to enable scrub jitter and lower concurrency. plan:
```
# rollout plan (hotfix)
- toggle janitor.deepScrubConcurrency -> 1
- enable janitor.scrubJitterRangeSeconds -> 600
- enable attach admission: gate if metric free_scratch_slots < 4
```
maria: timeline? we need to unblock GPU attaches ASAP (customers impacted).
liam: patch built, testing on one canary region now (eu-west1-a). if green, roll to pool in 5m. will also add a temporary scheduler admission rule to defer attach if attach-queue > 50 per-AZ.
sre-bot: NOTE: scheduled change window set by liam at 4169001248. automated rollback at 4169001408 if errors > 5% on attach success.
anya: also recommend increasing monitoring granularity for `free_scratch_slots` and instrumenting per-node scrub start time (to verify jitter spread). add alert: `free_scratch_slots < 10 for 10m` -> P1.
jordan: FYI cost note — pausing deep-scrubs will push some work later, might increase spot GPU attach latency slightly later, but fine tradeoff to keep current SLAs.
maria: agreed. can someone post the exact kubectl patch/commands you'll run? ops needs to know the rollout steps.
liam: commands i'm running on controlplane: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config --patch '{"data":{"deepScrubConcurrency":"1","scrubJitterRangeSeconds":"600","skipDeepScrubIfScratchBusy":"true"}}'
# then: curl -X POST https://provisioner.internal/api/v1/admiters/attach -d '{"policy":"free_scratch_slots>=4"}'
```
liam: deployed to canary at 4169001255. monitoring spike drop now visible; attach-queue down from 184 -> 22 in 60s.
maria: nice. propagation plan? how long to wait before AZ-wide roll?
liam: give it 3m on canary, then staggered rollout by AZ with 30s spacing between controlplane patches to avoid simultaneous scrub shifts. full rollout ETA 10m.
anya: I'll update runbook and add post-incident task: "investigate why scrub jitter was disabled for this pool". set owner: infra/storage.
jordan: follow-up: propose longer-term fix — make attach admission consider per-node nvme_iops_capacity and predicted janitor schedule; maybe soft-reserve slots for critical attaches.
maria: good action items. for now, monitor customer impact and keep this thread updated. thanks team. :thumbsup:
